llm.summary: The skill advertises a narrow Amazon seller action-plan helper but ships a much broader authenticated ARI account tool that can change settings, start recurring monitoring, consume credits, and write exports.

dimensions.detail: allowed-tools is Bash, and the bundled script gives the agent access to broad authenticated ARI account operations and local export writes, which is not proportionate to a narrow action-plan skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no dependency installer or remote code execution path found; setup/configure use a browser/device or hidden-input flow and save an ARI API key locally, and outbound requests are pinned to https://ari.funewa.com with redirect blocking.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation says the specialized entry must not switch workflow or accept arbitrary prompts, but operations quote/run accept --workflow and --focus and operation_payload gives those command-line values precedence over skill-defaults.json.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can persist an API key in ~/.ari/config.json and the script can change server-side persistent state such as schedule, competitor, watch, workbench status, and autoconfirm settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md describes a fixed single-ASIN audit/action planning workflow, while scripts/ari.py exposes a general ARI CLI with collection, generic analysis, reports, watches, competitors, schedules, alerts, workbench, leaderboard, autoconfirm, and export commands.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the agent Bash access to a broad ARI account CLI, not just a narrow action-plan helper. Use a restricted ARI token if available, review every command before confirmation, keep autoconfirm off for paid actions, and avoid export paths that could overwrite important files.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Upheld in substance: the declared purpose is narrow, but the shipped CLI surface is broad and includes account-level and paid-service operations not disclosed as part of the action-plan workflow.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: the references to scripts/ari.py are expected CLI references, and the referenced script was present locally and inspected.
[LP1] unexpected: Partly upheld: authenticated outbound requests to the ARI service are expected for this integration, but the available endpoints go well beyond the disclosed fixed action-plan use case.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Upheld: the broad account-management, monitoring, export, workbench, and analysis functions are not necessary for the declared single-ASIN action-plan workflow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Upheld: schedule, competitor, watch, autoconfirm, credential storage, and export behavior introduce persistent account or local-file effects that are under-scoped for this package.
[EA2] unexpected: Upheld: autoconfirm state can be read and modified, and some non-specialized flows can auto-confirm small paid operations, which is not aligned with a planning-only skill.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded for security verdict: Chinese-language documentation and defaults are visible to the user and do not by themselves show hidden or unsafe behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: Not material here: the default prompt is short but still points to an Amazon ASIN action plan; the larger issue is the bundled CLI authority, not invocation wording alone.
[T05] unexpected: Upheld: direct inspection confirmed authenticated commands for schedule, competitors, watches, workbench status, autoconfirm, collection, exports, and paid analyses beyond the declared scope.
[T09] unexpected: Upheld: workflow/focus can override packaged defaults, and export uses a caller-controlled --out path with truncating file writes.
